Ironic voice ('we will let it slide') that speaks as the enforcement agencies. Read sincerely, the expectation that health plans escape enforcement names no plan, case, agency action or period ('as UHG did 7 days ago' is a past aside), so no event could be written even then (VAGUE fallback).

'This case will be about the books' characterizes the content of the indictment, which the press release the author annotates already states (the IRS-CI quote). 'Easy to prove' is an assessment of difficulty, not an asserted outcome (conviction, plea, sentence). No observable event can be written without inventing a verdict.

'Every DEA license involved could be pulled': the universal quantifier has no countable set in the words. The author names no registrant, and 'involved' covers an unenumerated group of prescribers. 'Let's see some real consequences, DOJ' is a wish. Writing 'at least one revocation' would invent a threshold. 'Could' would have set bin C.

'This sets a standard' for how short a telehealth contact may be: no body (court, DEA, state board), instrument (rule, ruling, guidance) or threshold is named. 'Other virtual care providers are watching closely' is present tense. Nothing observable can be written.

'A lot of cover-up, I'll bet' is a magnitude claim about what the case will show, with no threshold, count or resolution source. The obstruction allegation itself is already in the indictment. 'I'll bet' would have set bin B.

Mixed normative and predictive claim: only prison and financial ruin 'will ... discourage capital from flowing to nitwits like this'. No countable set of ventures, series or threshold. 'In the future' is not a deadline.

'Limited faith that state medical boards will do much here': 'much' has no threshold, the boards ('especially in California') and the licensees are not enumerated, and no period is given. Writing 'at least one disciplinary action by the Medical Board of California' would invent the threshold. 'Limited faith' would have mapped to bin D.

event.title: Second Done Global / Mindful Mental Wellness indictment ends without any conviction
event.proposition: The court dismisses all charges against, or acquits, every defendant in the December 2025 federal indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A., so the case ends without any conviction or guilty plea.
event.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the order or verdict that disposes of the last remaining count in the December 2025 federal indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A. (the indictment announced in the DOJ press release the post annotates), if by that date no defendant in that indictment has been convicted at trial or has entered a guilty plea to any count. FALSE on the date of the first conviction or guilty plea of any defendant in that indictment. A superseding indictment in the same case is the same case. Resolution source: the federal court docket for the case (PACER, via CourtListener), with DOJ press releases as a secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Federal court docket for the December 2025 Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A. indictment (PACER via CourtListener); DOJ press releases

readings: 'This will go that far south' is read, from the DOJ boilerplate it reacts to (an indictment is only an allegation; defendants are presumed innocent), as the case ending with no defendant found guilty or pleading guilty.
'This' = the new (December 2025) indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A., not the earlier case in which the founders Ruthia He and David Brody were convicted.
A partial outcome (some defendants convicted, others acquitted or dismissed) is not 'that far south': the event requires no conviction or guilty plea at all.

records.phrase: I doubt this will go that far south
records.stage_note: The indictment was newly announced at the statement date (DOJ press release, December 2025); no trial, plea or dismissal yet. No class in base-rates.json covers the outcome of a federal criminal case, so b is null. Undated: 24-month window from 2025-12-18.
records.note: The forecaster doubts that the new case collapses. 'I doubt' is a lexicon D phrase applied to the doubted event, so bin D with asserts true and p(E) = 0.3 (house convention for D phrases, as in owen-1215). The doubted event is written positively as dismissal or acquittal of every defendant. 'Due process is due to all' is a normative aside, not coded. No time words, so undated (24-month window); a case still pending at the window end resolves as not occurred. The court and the DOJ decide; the forecaster holds no disclosed role in Done Global, Mindful Mental Wellness P.A. or the DOJ, so not affiliated. Not KNOWN: the press release announces charges, not a disposition. In area (regulatory): the case concerns the prescribing of stimulants for ADHD, psychiatric drugs, through a telehealth psychiatry provider, so its disposition is an enforcement outcome about the prescribing of and access to psychiatric treatment, not an unrelated legal outcome.

Sarcastic first sentence; the sincere claim is that insurers will not have 'plenty of in network stimulant prescribers' for displaced Done patients. 'Plenty' is a quantifier without a threshold, 'insurance company' has no countable set, and no network-adequacy series or period is named. 'I doubt' would have set bin D.
Near-truism: 'many adults will still have ADHD, and will need treatment' has no countable set, threshold, series or event. 'Many' is a quantifier without a set. Nothing can be written.

'This will similarly go well... oh, wait' is marked sarcasm. The intended meaning (the 988 redirection will not go well) is the opposite of the words, and it has no observable event or benchmark either (VAGUE fallback).

New York's aid-in-dying law is general end-of-life health policy, not a drug, device or treatment in psychiatry or the payment for or access to one; the claim concerns psychiatric patients' access to MAiD, not to psychiatric treatment. Outside the five areas as defined in the OUT_OF_AREA test. Would also be VAGUE: 'leaves the door wide open' is a present-tense reading of the statute, 'many of those individuals will have personality disorders' describes a population, and no public series records qualifying psychiatric diagnoses for a MAiD death or prescription.

A general pattern of aid-in-dying eligibility expansion ('then it expands to others') applied implicitly to New York's end-of-life law: general health policy, not a psychiatric drug, device or treatment or the payment for or access to one. Would also be VAGUE: no mechanism (amendment, ruling, practice drift), body, threshold or period is given.

MAiD use in New York 'ramps up' is a claim about a general end-of-life law, not about a psychiatric treatment or the payment for or access to one. Would also be VAGUE: 'a problem' and 'ramps up' name no metric, threshold, series or period, and the author names no reporting source. 'I suspect' would have set bin B.

'Hundreds of people who are going to apply' for aid in dying under the New York law: the subject is access to MAiD, a general end-of-life measure, not a psychiatric drug, device or treatment. Would also be VAGUE: applications by chronically suicidal, non-terminal people are not a reported quantity, no source is named, and no period is given. 'Are going to' would have set bin A.

'More people are gonna die by their own choosing' under the New York aid-in-dying law: a mortality claim about a general end-of-life measure, outside the five areas. Would also be VAGUE: a comparative without a benchmark, population, series or period; 'more humane for some' is a value judgment.

Moral claim in hyperbolic form about whom the New York aid-in-dying law will 'consign' to death: general end-of-life policy, not a psychiatric treatment or its payment or access. Would also be VAGUE: no countable set, threshold, resolution source or period.

Malpractice exposure of physicians who treat suicidal patients is a psychiatric-practice subject, so in area, but 'medical malpractice claims await' has no plaintiff, defendant, court, count or period. A quantifier without a countable set; 'await' is not a deadline.

'This will end as poorly as it has in every other place' concerns the New York aid-in-dying law as a whole: general end-of-life policy, outside the five areas as defined in the OUT_OF_AREA test. The central claim of the post. Would also be VAGUE: a comparative with no metric, benchmark, series or period. 'Will' would have set bin A.

'Adding MAiD to the roster increases the rate of individuals who die in their youth' is a claim about mortality under a general end-of-life law, not about a psychiatric drug, device or treatment. Would also be VAGUE: the present-tense causal generalization names no series, age band, threshold or period; a coder who reads no future state at all would reject NOT_FORECAST.

Payment for psychiatric treatment is in area. A plea ('now, please') plus a conditional consequence ('it will reduce the spending on physician suicide assessments'): no payer, series, benchmark or period; 'spending on physician suicide assessments' is not a reported quantity, and the condition (broad coverage) is undefined. The predictive clause blocks a pure NORMATIVE code.

event.asset: ERISA fiduciary-breach litigation over employer group health plans that pleads mental health parity (MHPAEA) violations
event.entity: US federal district courts (complaint filed by plan participants, their counsel or the Department of Labor)
event.title: First ERISA fiduciary lawsuit citing mental health parity (MHPAEA) violations is filed
event.proposition: A lawsuit is filed in a US federal court that pleads an ERISA breach-of-fiduciary-duty claim against the sponsor or fiduciaries of an employer group health plan and cites violations of the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act as a basis for the breach.
event.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a complaint filed in a US federal district court within the window that (a) pleads a claim under ERISA for breach of fiduciary duty against the sponsor, plan committee or other named fiduciaries of an employer-sponsored group health plan over the plan's design or administration, whether brought by plan participants or by the Department of Labor, and (b) cites the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA, 'mental health parity') as a basis of the alleged breach, as shown by the complaint text. A suit only for denied benefits under ERISA section 502(a)(1)(B) against an insurer or administrator, a state-court suit, or an amended complaint in a case filed before the window does not count. Resolution source: federal court dockets on CourtListener (PACER), with legal press reports as a finding aid only.
readings: 'ERISA lawsuit' is read, from the post's discussion of the Schlichter Bogard fiduciary-breach suits against employers (United Airlines, CHS, Universal Services of America, LabCorp), as a fiduciary-breach suit against a plan sponsor or its fiduciaries, not a benefit-denial suit against an insurer.
'The first' is read as 'at least one such suit is filed within the window'; the ledger does not verify that none existed before the statement date.
'Referencing mental health parity violations' = the complaint cites MHPAEA (or 'mental health parity') as a basis of the fiduciary breach.

records.phrase: will be filed. ... It happens in 2026
records.stage_note: At the statement date the author reports a batch of ERISA fiduciary suits against employers over health plans (Schlichter Bogard, filed the prior week) but none that cites MHPAEA. No class in base-rates.json covers the filing of a lawsuit, so b is null.
records.note: Item 1 of a predictions list published on 1 January 2026. 'Will be filed' and the flat 'It happens in 2026' set bin A, asserts true. 'In 2026' and the 1 January list both anchor the deadline at 2026-12-31. Plaintiffs, their counsel or the Department of Labor decide whether to file; the author only advocates ('I have been arguing that this is a good case to bring'), so not CONTROL. Filing events resolve under court_outcome on the docket date, as in owen-0048 and owen-1269; unlike owen-1048 the claim is singular, typed and dated. No entity in the forecaster's affiliations is named, so not affiliated. In area (payer_policy): mental health parity (MHPAEA) governs payment for and access to psychiatric treatment, and the suit's subject is parity violations, not general plan fees (which would be an employment-benefits matter outside the areas).

'Becomes the hot new Venture Funding category' is a slogan: no series (tracker), threshold, ranking or definition of 'hot' is given, so nothing can be written on a named series. The author's affiliations (Radial, Neurolief) sit in the category, which would have made an admitted item affiliated. The 1 January list would have anchored 2026-12-31.

Two claims, both rejected, so one record. (a) '2026 doubles that number into AI-enabled BCI companies': 'that number' is the author's own tally (over 300m USD in 2025) of a self-defined set (Radial, Beckley Clinical, Stella Centers, Hope Therapeutics, Big Leap, Osmind, Everbright) that mixes clinic networks and device makers. No public series carries that category, and a tracker's BCI category would not match the baseline, so a threshold cannot be written on a named series without inventing the category boundary. (b) 'Additional dollars and deal flow into non-invasive devices' is a comparative without a benchmark. Not CONTROL: Radial (the author's employer) does not decide an aggregate category; an admitted item would have been affiliated. 'I think' would have set bin B; the 1 January list would have anchored 2026-12-31.
